newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler urges aggressive EU world farm trade role.
newsitem.headline: Fischler urges aggressive EU world farm trade role.

text.p: The European Union must take advantage of an expected expansion of world agricultural trade, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday.

"The Union must not stand idly by in the face of such prospects, we must endeavour not merely to maintain our position as the world's largest agricultural trading partner but to consolidate it where we can," Fischler said in a speech.
The EU must exploit market openings, which in the future can only be done by increasing unsubsidised exports, he told the Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS).
The next round of world farm trade negotiations, due to start by 1999, is expected to bring increased pressure for a further opening of markets and increased trade.
"The recent debate on the Farm Bill in the United States also pointed in that direction," Fischler noted.
But he added that Europe, and perhaps countries such as Japan, should ensure that action against environmental and social dumping is taken in the next world trade round.
Fischler sought to reassure EU farmers who are worried they may not survive if they are forced to compete at near world market prices.
World cereal prices were expected to rise, he said.

"Virtually everyone is forecasting favourable medium- and long-term prospects, particularly because of trends in world population and standards of living," he said. --Peter Blackburn Brussels Bureau +322 287 6830
